_readme: Rich evidence pool behind the CV: detailed project narratives with context, architecture, metrics and interview angles. This is what /tailor-cv-full, /cover-letter and /interview-prep draw on when the one-line CV bullets are not enough.

Built during onboarding interviews (20-30 minutes of questions per role) and extended in instalments afterwards. Copy to data/deep_experience.json and replace the fictional Alex Example content with your own.

Structure: 'roles' holds per-employer project deep-dives; 'experience_clusters' groups related work into themes with skills demonstrated and story angles; 'validation_questions' tracks what is still unconfirmed so future sessions can fill the gaps. You can add extra domain-specific sections (the shape is open); anything here is treated as evidence the tailoring system may cite.

roles.context: Mid-size B2B services company (~200 staff). Joined as the second analyst in a small operations team reporting to the Head of Operations; the team owns company reporting, process improvement and internal tooling decisions.

projects.name: Customer Onboarding Redesign
projects.summary: Led the process mapping and requirements work behind a redesign of customer onboarding, cutting average turnaround time by 30% across 5 departments.
projects.timeline: ~6 months (Jan 2025 - Jun 2025). Discovery workshops in the first 6 weeks, agreed future-state map by month 3, phased rollout through month 6.

problem_context.background: Onboarding a new customer touched sales, legal, finance, operations and support, with handoffs tracked in email. Average turnaround was 14 days and nobody owned the end-to-end picture.

previous_failures.details: An earlier attempt to coordinate via a shared spreadsheet died because nobody kept it current and it had no notion of ownership or deadlines.

projects.architecture: Documented the as-is process as a swimlane map (one lane per department, 40+ steps), then designed a future state with 4 explicit handoff points, a single intake form feeding a tracked queue, and automated status notifications. Implementation used the company's existing ticketing tool rather than new software.
implementation_details: Ran 8 discovery workshops across the 5 departments to capture the real process, not the documented one
Quantified the baseline from 6 months of ticket and email timestamps using Python, which turned an opinion debate into a data discussion
Wrote the requirements spec for the intake form and queue configuration, then tested it with 3 pilot customers before rollout
Built the before/after measurement dashboard so the 30% claim is based on like-for-like turnaround data
projects.team_dynamics: No formal authority: worked through the Head of Operations and one sponsor per department. The hardest part was legal, who saw the tracker as surveillance; resolved by letting them define their own stage names and SLAs.
projects.technical_depth: Python (Pandas) for the baseline timestamp analysis; process mapping notation; ticketing tool configuration. Deliberately low-tech implementation; the insight was process design, not software.
interview_angles: Using data to defuse an opinion-driven disagreement
Scoping discipline: shipping with existing tools instead of proposing a new system

projects.name: Monthly Reporting Automation
projects.summary: Replaced the manual monthly operations reporting pack with an automated Python and SQL pipeline, saving 10+ hours a week and halving month-end errors.

problem_context.background: The monthly pack was 9 Excel workbooks assembled by hand from CRM and finance exports. It consumed the last two days of every month and errors were regularly discovered after distribution.

projects.architecture: Python scripts pull from the CRM API and the finance database (read-only SQL), transform with Pandas, validate against a set of reconciliation rules, and publish to Power BI datasets. A scheduled job runs daily so month-end is just a review, not a build.
implementation_details: Negotiated read-only database access with IT, the single biggest unblock
Wrote reconciliation checks (row counts, control totals, orphaned records) that run before anything is published
Kept one legacy workbook alive in parallel for two cycles to prove the numbers matched before switching off the manual process
Documented the pipeline so a colleague could run and modify it; it survived my two-week absence untouched
projects.team_dynamics: Solo build with review from the finance manager, who was initially sceptical that automated numbers could be trusted; the parallel-run period converted them.
projects.technical_depth: Python (Pandas, requests), SQL (joins, window functions for period-over-period deltas), Power BI dataset design, scheduled execution and logging.
interview_angles: Building trust in automation with a parallel-run migration
Data quality as a first-class feature, not an afterthought
Quantified impact: 10+ hours a week, error rate halved

experience_clusters.name: Operations Analytics & Reporting Ownership
experience_clusters.summary: Owns the company's operational reporting end to end: the automated monthly pack, 12 self-serve dashboards, the KPI framework, and the data quality checks underneath them. The through-line is turning manual, error-prone reporting into automated, trusted, self-serve analytics.
evidence: Monthly pack automated: 10+ hours a week saved, errors halved
15-metric KPI framework presented monthly to leadership
interview_story_angles: From manual reporting to self-serve analytics: the 18-month arc
How you get non-technical stakeholders to trust automated numbers
Owning a metric framework used by leadership

validation_questions.description: Questions to answer in follow-up sessions to complete low-confidence entries and fill documentation gaps. The onboarding interview adds items here whenever the user is unsure of a number or detail.
general_questions: Exact baseline and post-redesign onboarding turnaround figures (currently '14 days' and '30% faster' from memory)
Which CRM and finance systems can be named publicly in interviews, and which should stay generic?
Confirm the overtime savings estimate (CAD 40,000) with the source calculation before using it in a cover letter
